title: Random forest guides experimentally checked rare-earth disilicate phase design
summary: A random-forest classifier trained on 114 curated multicomponent rare-earth disilicate compositions identified cation-radius descriptors associated with retained high-temperature phases. Six new compositions were synthesized and characterized by X-ray diffraction and microscopy, supporting the predicted phase assignments and composition rules within two related material systems. The study establishes a specific phase-design result, not demonstrated coating service performance. The training corpus and experimental sample are small; seven withheld composition checks do not establish broad extrapolation across ceramics.
ai_technology: Random forest phase classifier; SVM and artificial neural network comparators
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Science and Technology of China; Liaoning Academy of Materials; AECC Shenyang Liming AERO-ENGINE Science and Technology Co., Ltd.

evidence.tested: A 114-composition training corpus and repeated random splits supported model selection. Six compositions absent from that corpus were synthesized and their phase assignments checked by XRD and microscopy; a seven-sample leave-one-combination-out check was also reported.
evidence.unknown: Small curated corpus, imbalanced phase categories and limited independent compositions restrict extrapolation. Coating lifetime, corrosion performance and operational engine outcomes were not established by these phase-characterization experiments.
evidence.ai_role: Random forest learned phase categories from seven composition descriptors, prioritized mean cation radius and its dispersion, and predicted composition-dependent phases for subsequent synthesis and characterization.
